note: After the fall of Acre (1291), the Knights Hospitaller retreated to Cyprus, which they used as a base for another 20 years before conquering Rhodes (1309). Cyprus provided the order's headquarters, naval facilities, and recruitment grounds during the critical transition from a land-based military order to a maritime one. The order's presence in Cyprus also entangled it in the complex dynastic politics of the Lusignan kingdom — a relationship that both aided and complicated the order's development of its new Mediterranean naval role.

_quarry.structural_significance: Cyprus serves as the transitional base that enables the Hospitallers' transformation from a land-based crusading order to the dominant Christian naval power in the eastern Mediterranean; the Rhodes phase (1309–1522) makes the Hospitallers the primary barrier to Ottoman expansion into the central Mediterranean
